records.notes: F_el0 says Mehta 'transferred ownership' of the units to Sethi 'under a written bailment agreement' -- self-contradictory: a bailment by definition leaves ownership with the bailor and gives the bailee only custody/possession. As worded, Sethi already owns the goods, which defeats the entrustment-of-another's-property premise el0 is supposed to establish and undermines the whole s.405 theory (you cannot breach trust over your own property). fact_fit and coherent both FAIL on this internal contradiction; F_el1 and F_el2 are each clean on their own.

Minor structural oddity (not a content failure): the elements array carries an el3 'unknown' entry with no corresponding fact, though required_elements for this contract lists only 3 elements (0-2). Answer's abstain_reason phrasing ('misappropriation or conversion to own use') is generic s.405 language rather than this contract's specific 'uses or disposes' wording, but it still correctly conveys that the use/disposal element is unestablished.
Clean pair of facts: entrustment of the logbooks (el0) and Thorne's wilful non-intervention while Kovic removed pages (el1) are independently stated and each stays within its own element.
Narrative gives Rohan only an innocuous 'assists with logistics' role; nothing anywhere hints at misappropriation or suffered wrongdoing, so the el1 omission is genuine.

F_el1 ('Suresh Patel agreed to purchase ... solely because he was fraudulently induced by Vikram Mehta's false representation') is a near-verbatim restatement of the statutory inducement language rather than an independent factual mechanism (e.g. what Patel actually did/relied on) -- reads as provision paraphrase, failing the coherent test even though it does not bleed into other elements.

Same template flaw as t_ipc415_property_0023: F_el1 ('Thorne was fraudulently induced by this misrepresentation ... to proceed ... he would have otherwise rejected') restates the legal inducement conclusion rather than describing a concrete inducement fact. Both records follow an identical 3-fact scaffold (false claim / conclusory-inducement sentence / payment), suggesting a formulaic template rather than independently authored scenarios.

el0 (deception) is supposed to be omitted, but F_el1 itself states the act was one 'she would not have taken had she known the true status of the hull inspection' -- this necessarily implies Thorne gave Kovic a false account of the hull inspection status, i.e. it establishes the very deception el0 is meant to be missing. So F_el1 fails fact_fit (leaks el0) and the omission is not real (el0 is established, just not under its own F_el0 key); the abstention answer is therefore wrong to say deception is unestablished. F_el1's wording is also a near-paraphrase of the statutory 'intentionally induces ... to do ... they would not otherwise have done' language, failing coherent as well.

F_el1 establishes only personation (presenting Sethi's ID, claiming to be Sethi); nothing in the record shows property/advantage obtained by that personation, so the el0 (cheats) omission and abstention are genuine. Shares protagonist 'Rohan Mehta' and referenced person 'Vikram Sethi' with its contract-mate t_ipc416_0022 -- not a scenario duplicate (different setting/conduct/object) but reduces cast diversity across this contract's pair.

F_el0 ('falsely claimed to be the authorized agent of collector Vikram Sethi and thereby dishonestly induced the ... manager to release [the] watch') already contains the personation claim that el1 is supposed to independently establish, so it does not stay confined to el0. Substantively, claiming to be someone's 'agent'/'representative' is a misrepresentation of authority, not 'pretending to be, substituting for, or misrepresenting the identity of' that person as s.416 personation requires (contrast t_ipc416_0020, where Mehta literally presents Sethi's ID and says 'I am Vikram Sethi') -- this fact pattern reads more like ordinary cheating (s.415) than cheating by personation, so both fact_fit and coherent FAIL.

el1 (intends/knows the false info will cause the consequence) is supposed to be omitted, but F_el2 states Mehta gave the tip 'with the specific purpose of triggering a police raid ... to harass his former business partner ... knowing such official action would cause significant distress and reputational harm' -- that is el1's content (intent/knowledge as to the consequence) verbatim, not just el2's consequence. So F_el2 fails fact_fit (establishes el1 as well as el2), and the omission is not real: el1 is in fact established in the record, contradicting its 'unknown' status and the abstention answer.

F_el0 establishes only the deceitful-promotion-promise inducement; intercourse is never mentioned, so the omission is genuine. Flagged as a near-duplicate of t_bns69_0022: identical two-person cast (Rohan Mehta / Priya Sharma), same Pune logistics-firm employer relationship, and an almost identically worded opening narrative sentence ('were colleagues at Apex Logistics in Pune' vs 'were colleagues at a logistics firm in Pune'). The two records differ only in which deceit route is used (false promotion vs false marriage promise) and whether intercourse occurred -- a legitimate minimal control/omit pair in principle, but the shared cast and near-identical scene-setting sentence reduce scenario diversity.

F_el0 (false marriage promise, no intention to fulfil) and F_el1 (intercourse occurred) are each independently stated and confined to their own element. See duplicate note on t_bns69_0021 for the near-identical cast/narrative concern.

F_el0 ('While attending a conference in Bengaluru, Vikram Sethi intentionally instigated Elena Rostova to ... exfiltrate ... code from a server located in Singapore') already fully states both el1 (abetting conduct done in India -- 'attending a conference in Bengaluru') and el2 (act abetted located outside India -- 'server located in Singapore') within the same sentence, so it does not establish 'only' el0; F_el1 and F_el2 then just restate content already given in F_el0. Separately, F_el3 characterizes unauthorized outside access and data exfiltration as 'the offence of criminal breach of trust' -- but criminal breach of trust requires an entrustment/fiduciary relationship over the property, which is absent here (Rostova has no entrustment relation to the Singapore server/code); the described conduct is legally closer to theft or unauthorized computer access, so F_el3's legal characterization is a factual/legal-accuracy error, not merely a stylistic one.
F_el0 establishes only the husband relationship; no cruelty is mentioned anywhere, so the el1 omission is genuine.
F_el0 (husband/relative status) and F_el1 (Sunita's harassment/property-demand cruelty) are independently stated and each confined to its own element; a plausible dowry-harassment fact pattern.

F_el0 already states the India-situs and abroad-situs facts that F_el1/F_el2 merely repeat, and F_el3 mislabels unauthorized outside computer access as 'criminal breach of trust' with no entrustment relationship present.

Claiming to be someone's 'agent'/'representative' is misrepresentation of authority, not personation of that person's identity -- a poor fit for the cheating-by-personation contract, and F_el0/F_el1 overlap.
